data.title: Repeated words
data.solution:
array = input().replace('\\n',' ').split()
n = len(array)
index = 0
found = False

lowarr=[i.lower() for i in array]

while index<n-1:
    test = lowarr[index]
    if not any(map(str.isalpha, test)):
        index+=1
        continue

    i=index+1
    while i<n and lowarr[i]==test:
        i+=1

    if i>index+1:
        print(array[index])
        found=True
    index = i
if not found:
    print('No repeats!')
data.statement:
When proofreading, some people have a hard time time seeing repeats, especially if they're broken up onto different lines. The brain just ignores them.

Print all of the <<consecutively repeated>> words found in a string, one on each line, to help find such words when editing text.

For the purposes of this clash, a <<word>> is defined thus:
1) <<Words>> are separated by spaces and/or line breaks. Line breaks are always represented as {{\n}} (backslash + n) in this clash.
2) <<Words>> must contain at least one alphabetical character.
3) <<Words>> that contain non-alphabetic characters will count them as part of the <<word>>. E.g. {{it's}}

Rules:
1) Only one line of input is provided.
2) Ignore capitalization when comparing.
3) When outputting repeats, print the first <<word>> exactly as it originally appears.
4) If there are many consecutive <<words>> which repeat in one group, output only the first <<word>>.
5) Print each repeated <<word>> on its own line, in the order found.
6) If there are no repeats, write {{No repeats!}}.
